claim: CloudFront Anycast Static IPs are a small, static list of IP addresses that connect to all CloudFront edge locations globally, used for zero-rated billing and client-side allow-listing.
question: What are CloudFront Anycast Static IPs?

values.display: a set of static IP addresses that allow
zero-rated billing

evidence.quote: Anycast Static IPs from Amazon CloudFront are a set of static IP addresses that allow you to connect to all CloudFront edge locations globally. They provide a small, static list of IPs that can be used for use cases like zero-rated billing, where network providers waive data charges for specific IP addresses with appropriate agreements in place, and client-side allow-listing for enhanced security posture.

claim: All CloudFront features work with Anycast Static IPs except that legacy clients without SNI are not supported, Price Class All is required, and IPv6 must be disabled.
question: Which limits apply when a distribution uses CloudFront Anycast Static IPs?

values.display: Anycast Static IPs will not support legacy clients
You are required to use Price Class All
You must disable IPv6

evidence.quote: All CloudFront features work with Anycast with three notable exceptions: 1/ Anycast Static IPs will not support legacy clients that cannot support SNI, 2/ You are required to use Price Class All when using Anycast Static IPs, and 3/ You must disable IPv6 when using Anycast Static IPs.

claim: CloudFront Anycast Static IPs can be used with multiple distributions, but they must be in the same account.
question: Can one Anycast Static IP list be shared by distributions in different accounts?

values.display: but they must be in the same account

evidence.quote: You can use the Anycast Static IPs with multiple distributions, but they must be in the same account.

claim: CloudFront Anycast Static IPs cannot be limited to a certain geographic region; they are spread across geographic regions.

values.display: CloudFront Anycast will only be available with IPs

evidence.quote: No. CloudFront Anycast will only be available with IPs spread across geographic regions.

claim: You can point a zone apex (example.com) at a CloudFront distribution with a Route 53 ALIAS record, and Route 53 does not charge for queries to ALIAS records mapped to a CloudFront distribution.
question: How can the zone apex be mapped to a CloudFront distribution?

values.display: configure an ALIAS record that lets you map
Route 53 doesn't charge for queries to ALIAS records

evidence.quote: Using Amazon Route 53, AWS's authoritative DNS service, you can configure an ALIAS record that lets you map the apex or root (example.com) of your DNS name to your Amazon CloudFront distribution.
Route 53 doesn't charge for queries to ALIAS records that are mapped to a CloudFront distribution.

claim: With CloudFront Anycast Static IPs you can point an apex domain to a distribution using any DNS provider by creating standard A records.
question: How can the zone apex be mapped to CloudFront when you do not use Route 53?

values.display: point your apex domain to your CloudFront distribution
create standard A records

evidence.quote: Alternatively, with CloudFront's Anycast Static IPs, you can point your apex domain to your CloudFront distribution using any DNS provider. Simply create standard A records using the 3 static IP addresses provided by CloudFront.

claim: Dedicated IP Custom SSL gives each certificate a dedicated IP address at every edge location, so it works with clients that do not support SNI; SNI Custom SSL lets multiple domains serve SSL over the same IP address and works with most modern browsers.
question: How do SNI Custom SSL and Dedicated IP Custom SSL differ?

values.display: allocates dedicated IP addresses to serve your SSL
works with browsers and other clients that do
multiple domains to serve SSL traffic over

evidence.quote: Dedicated IP Custom SSL allocates dedicated IP addresses to serve your SSL content at each CloudFront edge location. Because there is a one to one mapping between IP addresses and SSL certificates, Dedicated IP Custom SSL works with browsers and other clients that do not support SNI.

SNI Custom SSL relies on the SNI extension of the Transport Layer Security protocol, which allows multiple domains to serve SSL traffic over the same IP address by including the hostname viewers are trying to connect to.

claim: CloudFront works with any origin server that holds the original versions of your content, static or dynamic, including non-AWS origins, and there is no additional charge to use a custom origin.
question: Can CloudFront use an origin server outside AWS, and does it cost extra?

values.display: works with any origin server that holds
no additional charge to use a custom origin

evidence.quote: Yes. Amazon CloudFront works with any origin server that holds the original, definitive versions of your content, both static and dynamic. There is no additional charge to use a custom origin.

claim: For every origin you can assign a backup origin that automatically serves traffic if the primary is unavailable, triggered by chosen HTTP 4xx and 5xx status codes, and the two origins can be any combination of AWS and non-AWS origins.
question: Which origins can be combined in a CloudFront origin failover pair?

values.display: you can assign a backup origin
any combination of AWS and non-AWS origins

evidence.quote: For every origin that you add to a CloudFront distribution, you can assign a backup origin that can be used to automatically serve your traffic if the primary origin is unavailable. You can choose a combination of HTTP 4xx/5xx status codes that, when returned from the primary origin, trigger the failover to the backup origin. The two origins can be any combination of AWS and non-AWS origins.

claim: CloudFront supports content sent using the HTTP or WebSocket protocols, including dynamic pages, static files and live or on-demand media streaming over HTTP.
question: Which protocols and content types does CloudFront support?

live or on-demand media streaming over HTTP

Amazon CloudFront also supports delivery of live or on-demand media streaming over HTTP.

claim: AWS says to use invalidation only in unexpected circumstances; if files need to be removed from cache often, use a versioning system and/or a short expiration period.
question: When does the CloudFront FAQ recommend invalidation instead of versioning?

values.display: use invalidation only in unexpected circumstances
implement a versioning system for your files

evidence.quote: You should use invalidation only in unexpected circumstances; if you know beforehand that your files will need to be removed from cache frequently, it is recommended that you either implement a versioning system for your files and/or set a short expiration period.

claim: The CloudFront geo restriction feature lets you specify countries in which users can access content, or countries in which they cannot, and responds to a viewer in a restricted country with HTTP status code 403 (Forbidden).
question: What does CloudFront return to a viewer in a restricted country?

values.display: HTTP status code 403 (Forbidden)
specify a list of countries in which

evidence.quote: Yes, the Geo Restriction feature lets you specify a list of countries in which your users can access your content. Alternatively, you can specify the countries in which your users cannot access your content. In both cases, CloudFront responds to a request from a viewer in a restricted country with an HTTP status code 403 (Forbidden).
